sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店做DJ时，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带上300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: Welcome to the Daily Sunday Special.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《周日特别节目》。

sentences.en: I'm Gilbert Cruz, the editor of the New York Times Book Review, and every week I'm here with my colleagues.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报书评》编辑吉尔伯特·克鲁兹，每周我都会和我的同事们在这里交流。

sentences.en: We're talking about music and movies and books and TV, just all sorts of fun stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们聊音乐、电影、书籍、电视，各种有趣的话题。

sentences.en: Today, we're talking about fashion.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要聊聊时尚。

sentences.en: This month kicked off the big four fashion weeks, New York, London, Milan and Paris.
sentences.zh: 本月开启了四大时装周：纽约、伦敦、米兰和巴黎。

sentences.en: And if you've ever seen even a single photo from one of these runways, I think you know that those clothes bear little resemblance to what we wear on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 如果你看过这些秀场上的任何一张照片，我想你一定知道，那些衣服和我们日常穿的几乎没什么关系。

sentences.en: But those clothes and those events are still important and influential in many ways.
sentences.zh: 但这些服装和活动在很多方面依然重要且具有影响力。

sentences.en: I want to know how, and today we're going to talk about that.
sentences.zh: 我想知道原因，今天我们就来聊聊这个。

sentences.en: And we're also going to answer some of your questions about personal style.
sentences.zh: 我们还会回答一些关于个人风格的问题。

sentences.en: With me today are two of my colleagues who cover fashion for The Times, Stella Bugbee, the editor of our Styles Desk.
sentences.zh: 今天和我一起的是两位负责《纽约时报》时尚报道的同事，我们的风格版块编辑斯特拉·巴格比。

sentences.en: Hello, Stella.
sentences.zh: 你好，斯特拉。

sentences.en: Hello, Gilbert.
sentences.zh: 你好，吉尔伯特。

sentences.en: Also here is Jacob Gallagher, who is one of our fashion reporters, who goes to a lot of Fashion Week events.
sentences.zh: 还有雅各布·加拉格尔，他是我们的时尚记者之一，经常参加时装周活动。

sentences.en: Hello, Jacob.
sentences.zh: 你好，雅各布。

sentences.en: Hi, Gilbert.
sentences.zh: 嗨，吉尔伯特。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So I feel like I have to fess up straight away.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我得先坦白一下。

sentences.en: Maybe you already know this based on what I wear around the office.
sentences.zh: 也许从我平时在办公室的穿着你们已经看出来了。

sentences.en: But I don't feel like a particularly fashionable person.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己算不上一个特别时尚的人。

sentences.en: I don't follow the world of fashion.
sentences.zh: 我不关注时尚圈。

sentences.en: I don't think about it a ton.
sentences.zh: 我对此思考得也不多。

sentences.en: Not because I don't think it's important, but because it seems kind of impenetrable to me.
sentences.zh: 不是因为我觉得它不重要，而是因为它对我来说似乎有点难以捉摸。

sentences.en: It's a little like sports sometimes.
sentences.zh: 有时候感觉就像体育运动一样。

sentences.en: There's so many names to remember.
sentences.zh: 要记住的名字太多了。

sentences.en: So many designers.
sentences.zh: 设计师太多了。

sentences.en: I'm hoping that we can have a conversation that sort of unlocks that.
sentences.zh: 我希望我们能通过对话来解开这些困惑。

sentences.en: But I want to go way back firSt.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我想追溯到很久以前。

sentences.en: First, I want to ask each of you, when you think you first understood that fashion was not only important,
sentences.zh: 我想先问问你们两位，你们是什么时候意识到时尚不仅很重要，

sentences.en: but it's actually something that you wanted to spend your time thinking about.
sentences.zh: 而且是你真正想花时间去思考的东西的？

sentences.en: We're all pointing at each other.
sentences.zh: 我们都在指着对方。

sentences.en: This is a real Spider-Man meme here.
sentences.zh: 这简直就是现实版的蜘蛛侠互指梗。

sentences.en: I think what makes fashion interesting to me is that it's about how we like to be perceived out in the world and the messages that we like to send.
sentences.zh: 我认为时尚之所以吸引我，是因为它关乎我们希望在世界上如何被看待，以及我们想要传递的信息。

sentences.en: And it's one way that we can decode the world around us neatly and easily.
sentences.zh: 这是我们解读周围世界的一种简洁明了的方式。

sentences.en: Or at least that's the hope, right?
sentences.zh: 或者至少我们希望如此，对吧？

sentences.en: You pick the clothes you pick to communicate sort of how you think you stand in the world if you can.
sentences.zh: 如果你能做到的话，你选择的衣服就是在传达你认为自己在世界上的位置。

sentences.en: I think I was very aware of that growing up in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 我在华盛顿特区长大时就对此深有体会，

sentences.en: where what you wear is very coded to where you fit into the world.
sentences.zh: 在那里，你的穿着直接对应了你在社会中的定位。

sentences.en: And as a very little child, I just remember thinking like, oh, it's very easy to tell which group everybody is a part of.
sentences.zh: 小时候我就记得自己想过：哦，要分辨每个人属于哪个群体太容易了。

sentences.en: There were the suits, the punks, the soccer moms, just these tribes of style choices that people would make.
sentences.zh: 有穿西装的、有朋克、有足球妈妈，人们通过风格选择形成了不同的部落。

sentences.en: And it had nothing to do with high fashion.
sentences.zh: 这和高级时装毫无关系。

sentences.en: And as a young, young child, I wasn't, you know, aware of trends or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 作为一个小孩子，我并不了解什么潮流之类的东西。

sentences.en: But I was very aware of the way people use fashion to display their values in the world.
sentences.zh: 但我非常清楚人们如何利用时尚来展示他们的价值观。

sentences.en: Gilbert, I'll maybe ask you to not use fashion as much as clothes.
sentences.zh: 吉尔伯特，我建议你把“时尚”换成“服装”来用。

sentences.en: Like, I'm sure a lot of listeners make that same distinction.
sentences.zh: 我相信很多听众也会做同样的区分。

sentences.en: But to me, like, what we do is cover clothes.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，我们报道的是服装。

sentences.en: Like, I think, and fashion is a part of that.
sentences.zh: 时尚只是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: Like, high fashion as you're perceiving it on the runway is certainly part of that.
sentences.zh: 你在秀场上看到的高级时装当然是其中一部分。

sentences.en: But, like, what we talk about is just the broad universe, landscape of clothes.
sentences.zh: 但我们讨论的是服装的广阔宇宙和全貌。

sentences.en: And so, like, I also grew up, I grew up right outside D.C.
sentences.zh: 我也是在华盛顿特区郊外长大的。

sentences.en: And I grew up in kind of the skateboarding, hardcore punk world.
sentences.zh: 我是在滑板和硬核朋克的世界里长大的。

sentences.en: And that is a very, you know, aesthetically driven space.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常注重美学的空间。

sentences.en: It's very tribal.
sentences.zh: 非常部落化。

sentences.en: How you dress dictates, you know, what you're into or who you're into.
sentences.zh: 你的穿着决定了你的喜好或你属于哪一类人。

sentences.en: And I think that was where the awareness came in for me.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是我最初产生这种意识的地方。

sentences.en: Like, I have a cousin who is from the Bay Area, which was its own punk scene.
sentences.zh: 我有个表亲来自湾区，那里有独特的朋克文化。

sentences.en: And I will always remember, in the way you always look up to your older cousins, he had a hoodie that he never washed.
sentences.zh: 我永远记得，就像你会崇拜年长的表亲一样，他有一件从不洗的连帽衫。

sentences.en: And it was disgusting.
sentences.zh: 那件衣服脏得要命。

sentences.en: But I thought it was the coolest thing on earth.
sentences.zh: 但我当时觉得它是世界上最酷的东西。

sentences.en: Because it was, like, from this band that he loved and he was really into that I didn't know of.
sentences.zh: 因为它来自他喜欢的一个我不知道的乐队，他非常迷那个乐队。

sentences.en: Because they were from the Bay Area.
sentences.zh: 因为他们来自湾区。

sentences.en: And that, I just remember the fact that it felt like that sweatshirt had something that made it greater.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时的感觉是，那件卫衣似乎拥有某种让它变得更伟大的特质。

sentences.en: And the fact that a piece of clothing and cotton stitched together could take on something like that, that registered with me pretty early.
sentences.zh: 一件棉质缝制的衣服能承载那样的意义，这种认知很早就植根于我心中了。

sentences.en: And I would say, to maybe try to answer your question in, like, the high fashion world, the first piece of high fashion I bought were a pair of Jinya Watanabe jeans
sentences.zh: 如果要回答你关于高级时装的问题，我买的第一件高级时装是渡边淳弥的牛仔裤，

sentences.en: that I bought when I was, like, I want to say 20.
sentences.zh: 那是我大概20岁的时候买的。

sentences.en: And I had just moved to New York.
sentences.zh: 我刚搬到纽约。

sentences.en: I transferred colleges.
sentences.zh: 我转学了。

sentences.en: I was in New York.
sentences.zh: 我在纽约。

sentences.en: I was working retail.
sentences.zh: 我在做零售工作。

sentences.en: And I saved up for these jeans.
sentences.zh: 我攒钱买了这条牛仔裤。

sentences.en: And I really, they looked like what you'd put on a scarecrow.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来就像你会给稻草人穿的那种。

sentences.en: Like, out in the, out on your farm.
sentences.zh: 就像在农场里那样。

sentences.en: Like, ready to stuff up straw.
sentences.zh: 准备往里面塞稻草的样子。

sentences.en: They were, like, really patched.
sentences.zh: 它们上面有很多补丁。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It was, like, they should have come with a packet of straw.
sentences.zh: 它们简直应该附赠一包稻草。

sentences.en: But they, to me, they felt, and I hate saying this word now because it's so cringe, but they felt very punk.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，它们感觉——我现在说这个词觉得很尴尬——但它们感觉非常朋克。

sentences.en: They felt like the high fashion version of what I grew up looking at and believing in and wanting to emulate.
sentences.zh: 它们感觉就像是我从小看到、相信并想要效仿的那种风格的高级时装版本。

sentences.en: And I still have them.
sentences.zh: 我至今还留着它们。

sentences.en: I refuse to get rid of them.
sentences.zh: 我拒绝扔掉它们。

sentences.en: They are now, like, way, way too small, but they, they're, they're so prized to me still.
sentences.zh: 虽然现在穿不上了，但我依然视若珍宝。

sentences.en: I think what you're getting at is, is one of my favorite terms, which is the narcissism of small differences, right?
sentences.zh: 我想你提到的是我最喜欢的术语之一，即“小差异的自恋”，对吧？

sentences.en: It's like this, this idea that you're going to notice that somehow my shirt is different than somebody else's shirt because you're going to be clued in to the secret messages
sentences.zh: 这是一种想法，你会注意到我的衬衫和别人的衬衫有何不同，因为你掌握了那些秘密信息，

sentences.en: that a junior Watanabe jeans might, you know, send out to the people who know what those things are.
sentences.zh: 比如渡边淳弥的牛仔裤可能会向懂行的人传递某种信号。

sentences.en: That's kind of what makes fashion sort of fun.
sentences.zh: 这正是时尚有趣的地方。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: What happened to your cousin's sweatshirt?
sentences.zh: 你表亲的那件卫衣后来怎么样了？

sentences.en: Oh, man, I'd have to ask him.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我得去问问他。

sentences.en: Did he ever wash it?
sentences.zh: 他洗过吗？

sentences.en: He, he, he definitely did wash it at some point or it's just disintegrated.
sentences.zh: 他肯定在某个时候洗过，或者它已经彻底烂掉了。

sentences.en: It's now in a landfill out near Benicia, California.
sentences.zh: 现在它可能在加州贝尼西亚附近的垃圾填埋场里。

sentences.en: He never washed it.
sentences.zh: 他从来没洗过。

sentences.en: He never washed it.
sentences.zh: 他从来没洗过。

sentences.en: Well, you know, I mean, also like there was a time where this is a total tangent, but in like clothing, you know, the whole thing was to never wash your jeans and they could,
sentences.zh: 好吧，你知道，还有一段时间——这完全是题外话——在服装界，你知道，当时流行的是永远不要洗牛仔裤，它们最终可以，

sentences.en: you know, eventually walk out the door on their own.
sentences.zh: 你知道，自己站着走出门去。

sentences.en: But they, I, I tried to never do that, but I wonder if he was just ahead of the curve maybe on the raw denim movement a little bit, but.
sentences.zh: 但我尽量不那样做，不过我在想他是不是在原色牛仔裤运动方面领先了一步。

sentences.en: I feel like we all had that cousin.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们都有过那样的表亲。

sentences.en: Oh, totally.
sentences.zh: 哦，完全同意。

sentences.en: That you looked up to totally.
sentences.zh: 那种你完全崇拜的表亲。

sentences.en: It's, it's always a cousin.
sentences.zh: 总是表亲。

sentences.en: It's never a sibling, you know.
sentences.zh: 从来不是亲兄弟姐妹，你知道的。

sentences.en: As we speak, New York Fashion Week has ended.
sentences.zh: 就在我们说话的时候，纽约时装周已经结束了。

sentences.en: Stella, you are shortly going to head over to Paris Fashion Week.
sentences.zh: 斯特拉，你很快就要前往巴黎时装周了。

sentences.en: Is that correct?
sentences.zh: 对吗？

sentences.en: I am.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So speaking for myself, I have little idea what goes on at these events.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我不太了解这些活动到底在干什么。

sentences.en: I see videos.
sentences.zh: 我看到视频。

sentences.en: I see photos.
sentences.zh: 我看到照片。

sentences.en: I imagine various celebrities sitting in various places and watching models walk down the runway.
sentences.zh: 我能想象各种名人在各种地方坐着，看着模特走秀。

sentences.en: But I actually don't know what any of that means.
sentences.zh: 但我其实不知道这一切意味着什么。

sentences.en: I don't understand what's happening in the room.
sentences.zh: 我不明白房间里到底在发生什么。

sentences.en: I would love for you to decode it for me a little bit, if you can, as someone who's been to maybe more than a few of these.
sentences.zh: 如果你能作为一个参加过很多次这种活动的人，为我解读一下，我会非常感激。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I, I don't think that I understood before I started going to fashion shows exactly what the purpose of fashion shows were.
sentences.zh: 我想在开始参加时装秀之前，我也不完全理解时装秀的目的。

sentences.en: They are both to display new ideas for that season or for the coming opposite season.
sentences.zh: 它们既是为了展示当季或即将到来的反季节的新创意。

sentences.en: So if it's fall, we're looking at spring of the following year.
sentences.zh: 所以如果是秋季，我们看的是次年春季的款式。

sentences.en: If it's spring, you're looking at fall.
sentences.zh: 如果是春季，你看的就是秋季的。

sentences.en: And the show is supposed to preview for editors and members of the press, as well as buyers for major department stores and smaller stores, you know, what's going to be available.
sentences.zh: 时装秀旨在为编辑、媒体成员以及大型百货公司和小型商店的买手预展即将上市的产品。

sentences.en: And so the buyers will go to the show and then they will do an appointment after the show and pick which things they're going to bring into their stores.
sentences.zh: 买手们会参加时装秀，然后在秀后进行预约，挑选他们要引入商店的款式。

sentences.en: The editors will go to the show and they will ostensibly decide which looks they're going to photograph in the pages of their magazines.
sentences.zh: 编辑们会参加时装秀，表面上他们会决定要在杂志页面上拍摄哪些造型。

sentences.en: That was how it used to work.
sentences.zh: 过去就是这样运作的。

sentences.en: And that's pretty much still the format that we all follow.
sentences.zh: 这基本上仍然是我们大家遵循的模式。

sentences.en: Am I missing anything, Jacob?
sentences.zh: 我漏掉了什么吗，雅各布？

sentences.en: Well, I would say, I think it's important to parse out that the buyer interaction has in many cases, like that's withered, I would say, like, because a lot of, as you kind of
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想说，解析一下买手互动在很多情况下已经萎缩是很重要的，因为正如你所暗示的，吉尔伯特，

sentences.en: alluded to actually, Gilbert, like for some brands, what they show is purely conceptual.
sentences.zh: 对于某些品牌来说，他们展示的东西纯粹是概念性的。

sentences.en: It will never be shown to buyers.
sentences.zh: 它永远不会展示给买手看。

sentences.en: It will never be purchased.
sentences.zh: 它永远不会被购买。

sentences.en: It will never land in stores.
sentences.zh: 它永远不会出现在商店里。

sentences.en: I think people focus maybe a little too much on that aspect, but there is no denying that the purpose of it, I think, is now more as marketing exercise than as a way to drum
sentences.zh: 我认为人们可能在这一方面关注得有点太多了，但不可否认的是，我认为它的目的现在更多是一种营销手段，而不是为了激发商业兴趣，

sentences.en: up interest for the commercial side of your business or to get, you know, to try to offer catnip to those buyers.
sentences.zh: 或者试图向那些买手提供诱饵。

sentences.en: I think now it's like the event itself is the marketing end.
sentences.zh: 我觉得现在活动本身就是营销的终点。

sentences.en: And you see that in, like, reports about how much, like, marketing dollars these shows equate to and what have you.
sentences.zh: 你可以从关于这些时装秀等同于多少营销预算的报道中看出这一点。

sentences.en: And that's why they invite celebrity and all that.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他们邀请名人等等。

sentences.en: But I think it still functions the same as, like, a member of the press in a way.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它在某种程度上仍然像媒体成员一样发挥作用。

sentences.en: You're still looking at it, trying to dissect, like, what this might mean for the broader market.
sentences.zh: 你仍然在观察它，试图剖析这对更广阔的市场意味着什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, like, what are the trends going to be?
sentences.zh: 是的，比如潮流会是什么？

sentences.en: I think that's the big question coming out of each season.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是每一季之后最大的问题。

sentences.en: That, at least traditionally, has been there.
sentences.zh: 至少传统上是这样。

sentences.en: Traditionally.
sentences.zh: 传统上。

sentences.en: I wouldn't say that it's so predictive.
sentences.zh: 我不会说它那么具有预测性。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想你是对的。

sentences.en: I think, like, the glamour that you're seeing, if I can kind of try to bring you in the room.
sentences.zh: 我想，如果你能让我带你进入那个房间，你所看到的魅力，

sentences.en: Please do.
sentences.zh: 请务必带我进去。

sentences.en: The glamour that you're seeing is really not what we're experiencing.
sentences.zh: 你所看到的魅力其实并不是我们所经历的。

sentences.en: It's like, if you've ever waited for the bus, or if you've ever been at a concert, and you've been like, why will this band just not go on already?

sentences.zh: 现在很难回答这个问题，因为我不认为你可以合理地说存在一个趋势，甚至五个趋势。

sentences.en: What's, what's in, what's, what are the trends?
sentences.zh: 是的，T台上可能会有很多蕾丝之类的东西，但这并不一定意味着会出现蕾丝趋势。

sentences.en: And it's really hard to answer that now because I don't think that you could reasonably say there is one or there are even five.
sentences.zh: 它不再是那样运作的了。

sentences.en: Yes, there may be a lot of lace on the runway or something like that, but it doesn't necessarily mean that there's going to be a lace trend.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，高级时尚运作的方式，奢侈时尚现在运作的方式，它必须是广泛可接受的。

sentences.en: It's, it doesn't work that way anymore.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些拥有这些小型时尚品牌的公司，你的Louis Vuitton，你的Dior，你的Saint Laurent，你的Balenciaga，它们必须在全球范围内取得成功。

sentences.en: But I also think that like the way that high fashion works, the way that luxury fashion works now, it has to be broadly palatable.
sentences.zh: 当你以如此大的规模运营，并且必须继续以惊人的速度创造收入时，你不会在店内提供那么革命性的想法。

sentences.en: And what I mean by that is these corporations that own these smaller fashion labels, your
sentences.zh: 我认为这对大公司以及，你知道，你的大型主流时尚品牌，你的Levi's，你的Gap，你的Uniqlo在某种程度上都是如此。

sentences.en: Louis Vuittons, your Dior's, your St. Laurent's, your Balenciaga's, they have to be globally successful.
sentences.zh: 所以你不得不继续给消费者他们已经买单的东西。

sentences.en: And when you are operating at that big of a scale and you have to continue to generate revenue at an incredible clip, you don't offer as revolutionary of ideas within the store.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，要彻底改变那个消费者并创造兴奋感，让人们真正相信他们需要支持它，变得越来越难了。

sentences.en: And that's true both for, I think, the huge companies as well as like, you know, your big
sentences.zh: 我觉得服装和其他文化、其他流行文化之间有很多相似之处，也就是，你知道，公司说，

sentences.en: mainstream fashion labels, your, you know, Levi's, your Gaps, your Uniqlo's to an extent.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这些类型的电影或这些类型的电视节目有大众受众。

sentences.en: And so you kind of have to keep giving the consumer what they're buying into already.
sentences.zh: 因此，这就是我们需要迎合的东西。

sentences.en: And so it does become harder and harder to, I think, revolutionize that consumer and create excitement and have people really believe they need to get behind that.
sentences.zh: 我们需要制作它最可口的形式，因为我们在这里是为了赚钱，

sentences.en: I feel like there are so many analogs here between clothing and other sorts of culture, other kinds of pop culture, which is, you know, the, the corporations, companies say,
sentences.zh: 而高级艺术形式或实验可能不是我们要投资的东西。

sentences.en: we know there's a mass audience out there for these type of movies or these type of TV shows.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我还要说的是，对我来说，当我成长的时候，我的穿衣方式是我所沉迷的亚文化的反映。

sentences.en: Therefore, that is the thing we need to cater to.
sentences.zh: 我认为现在孩子们穿衣的方式在很多方面是他们所沉迷的衣服的反映，如果这说得通的话。

sentences.en: We need to make the most palatable form of it because we are here to make money and
sentences.zh: 就像是衣服本身就是人们感兴趣的东西，也是他们从中汲取灵感的东西。

sentences.en: high forms of art or experimentation maybe is not the thing that we are going to invest in.
sentences.zh: 而且它们与最初的亚文化背景非常脱节。

sentences.en: Well, I would also say for me, when I was growing up, like the way I dress was a reflection of the subculture that I was into.
sentences.zh: 所以这最终导致了，你现在看到了这种奇怪的反馈循环，街上的孩子们，我们这里说的“孩子”范围很广，

sentences.en: I think now the way kids dress in a lot of ways is a reflection of the clothes they're into, if that makes any sense.
sentences.zh: 比如街上20多岁的人，青少年，穿得非常像90年代，那种宽松裤子配露脐上衣的风格。

sentences.en: It's like that, that like the clothes themselves are what people are interested in and what they're pulling from.
sentences.zh: 这就像是衣服本身就是人们感兴趣的东西，也是他们从中汲取灵感的东西。

sentences.en: And they're very removed from their original subcultural context.
sentences.zh: 而且它们与最初的亚文化背景非常脱节。

sentences.en: So that ends up resulting in like, you're seeing this weird feedback loop right now where like kids on the street, kids, we're using kids very loosely.
sentences.zh: 所以这最终导致了，你现在看到了这种奇怪的反馈循环，街上的孩子们，我们这里说的“孩子”范围很广，

sentences.en: Let's say like 20 something people on the street, teenagers are dressing very like 90s, like the baggy pant crop top thing.
sentences.zh: 比如街上20多岁的人，青少年，穿得非常像90年代，那种宽松裤子配露脐上衣的风格。

sentences.en: And then that I think is then feeding back into fashion and you're seeing designers then try to give that directly to that audience.
sentences.zh: 我认为这反过来又在影响时尚，你会看到设计师们试图直接向这些受众提供他们想要的东西。

sentences.en: So they're trying basically to make money by pulling from how these kids are dressing.
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上是想通过借鉴这些年轻人的穿搭方式来赚钱。

sentences.en: I think we're, I like to call my kids who are Gen Z, like Gen Z chaos fashion.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们，我喜欢把我这些Z世代的孩子们称为“Z世代混乱时尚”。

sentences.en: It's just, it has.
sentences.zh: 就是这样，确实如此。

sentences.en: Have you officially branded this as this?
sentences.zh: 你正式给它贴上这个标签了吗？

sentences.en: With them?
sentences.zh: 和他们一起吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I love how chaotic they are.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢他们那种混乱的感觉。

sentences.en: They're truly chaotic.
sentences.zh: 他们确实很混乱。

sentences.en: Like there's no, I look at the choices they make and I'm like, I don't understand what's informing this.
sentences.zh: 就像没有逻辑一样，我看着他们的选择，心想，我不明白是什么在影响这些决定。

sentences.en: And I don't think they do.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得他们自己也不明白。

sentences.en: And I think that that's what I mean when I say post consensus.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所说的“后共识”的意思。

sentences.en: But I keep thinking about norm core, which was a little over 10 years ago, a pretty big movement that was, I think, a rejection of individuality.
sentences.zh: 但我一直在想“极简主义”（norm core），那大约是十多年前的事了，当时是一个相当大的运动，我认为那是对个性的一种排斥。

sentences.en: And that didn't come from fashion, but it was expressed often through fashion, which is just this, everything is generic and you're one of 7 billion.
sentences.zh: 那并非源于时尚界，但通常通过时尚来表达，就是那种“一切皆平庸，你只是70亿分之一”的感觉。

sentences.en: And that has been hard to shake.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉很难摆脱。

sentences.en: Although I, when I talk about Gen Z chaos style, I think that that is the first time we're seeing kind of a rejection of norm core, which I think has been norm core being the
sentences.zh: 虽然当我谈论Z世代混乱风格时，我认为这是我们第一次看到对“极简主义”的某种排斥，我认为“极简主义”是

sentences.en: most prevailing aesthetic that we've seen in the last 10 years.
sentences.zh: 过去十年中我们见过的最流行的审美。

sentences.en: And whether that's in minimalist clothing or minimalist interiors or millennial pink or any of these big pervading aesthetics that have, that have like really changed interior
sentences.zh: 无论是极简风格的服装、极简主义的室内设计、千禧粉，还是任何这些已经真正改变了室内

sentences.en: design or have changed car design or shoe design or, you know, all of those things were related to that.
sentences.zh: 设计、汽车设计或鞋履设计的流行审美，你知道，所有这些事物都与此相关。

sentences.en: Now, I think we're seeing a more eclectic rejection of that desire to be anonymous.
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为我们正在看到一种更折衷的、对那种“想要隐身”的渴望的排斥。

sentences.en: People are, I think, finding their individuality again a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我觉得人们正在一点点找回他们的个性。

sentences.en: Okay, on that point, let's take a break.
sentences.zh: 好的，说到这一点，我们休息一下。

sentences.en: And when we come back, you all are going to answer some listener questions.
sentences.zh: 回来之后，你们将回答一些听众的问题。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 430 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空中的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟中最强的球队。

I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 庆祝175年来帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享受nytimes.com/subscribe的特别优惠。

sentences.en: A few weeks ago, we did a call out and we asked listeners to send us their personal style questions.
sentences.zh: 几周前，我们发出了征集，请听众发送他们关于个人风格的问题。

sentences.en: And we got so many responses.
sentences.zh: 我们收到了很多回复。

sentences.en: Thank you to everyone who submitted a question.
sentences.zh: 感谢每一位提交问题的人。

sentences.en: Obviously, we can't ask or answer them all.
sentences.zh: 显然，我们无法全部提问或回答。

sentences.en: So, I'm just going to put a few to Stella and Jacob and see what we get.
sentences.zh: 所以，我打算挑几个问问Stella和Jacob，看看会得到什么答案。

sentences.en: Are you guys ready?
sentences.zh: 你们准备好了吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 准备好了。

sentences.en: So, as I, so many questions, as I said.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，问题非常多。

sentences.en: And as I read through many of the questions, I saw that something that a lot of people had on their minds is how to dress for their age.
sentences.zh: 当我读到许多问题时，我发现很多人关心的一个问题是如何穿出符合自己年龄的风格。

sentences.en: People in their 60s, 70s, people in their 80s, but also listeners that were much younger than that.
sentences.zh: 有60多岁、70多岁、80多岁的人，也有比这年轻得多的听众。

sentences.en: And this first one is from Paul.
sentences.zh: 第一个问题来自Paul。

sentences.en: He lives in Rostock, Germany.
sentences.zh: 他住在德国罗斯托克。

sentences.en: Paul asks,
sentences.zh: Paul问：

sentences.en: I've been trying to find a more modern adult style for a while now, since I'm still wearing a similar style to the one I've been wearing since high school.
sentences.zh: 我一直在努力寻找一种更现代的成人风格，因为我穿的还是高中时期的那种风格。

sentences.en: I believe Paul is in his late 20s.
sentences.zh: 我想Paul应该快30岁了。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: And how can I change that?
sentences.zh: 我该如何改变呢？

sentences.en: I can answer the why easier than the how, I think.
sentences.zh: 我觉得回答“为什么”比回答“怎么做”要容易。

sentences.en: The why is that is because basically there's very little societal pressure today to dress in an adult manner, depending on your career.
sentences.zh: 之所以这样，是因为基本上现在社会上对于以成年人的方式着装的压力很小，这取决于你的职业。

sentences.en: But, you know, I think there is not the same pipeline of, like, you graduate school, you get a mature wardrobe as you move into the workforce.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，我认为现在已经没有那种“毕业后进入职场就得换上一套成熟衣橱”的固定流程了。

sentences.en: You don't need that anymore based on, I would say, the withering of dress codes in the corporate world.
sentences.zh: 由于企业界着装规范的式微，你不再需要那样做了。

sentences.en: It's very hard as a result, I feel, for Paul.
sentences.zh: 因此，我觉得这对Paul来说很难。

sentences.en: Like, I do understand that.
sentences.zh: 我确实理解这一点。

sentences.en: Like, it's hard to try to then dress in a way that feels better without feeling, like, risky.
sentences.zh: 想要尝试一种感觉更好但又不会显得“冒险”的穿搭方式，确实很难。

sentences.en: I get that tension.
sentences.zh: 我理解那种纠结。

sentences.en: I feel like we need to go back to the fundamental question.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们需要回到根本问题上。

sentences.en: Like, you said we got tons of questions about how to dress your age.
sentences.zh: 就像你说的，我们收到了大量关于如何穿出年龄感的提问。

sentences.en: And, you know, pulling back on that, it's so hard to age, period.
sentences.zh: 退一步讲，变老本身就很难。

sentences.en: We have, like, a ton of things to navigate psychologically around those questions, you know.
sentences.zh: 围绕这些问题，我们在心理上有很多东西需要应对，你知道的。

sentences.en: It's not just clothing.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是衣服的问题。

sentences.en: It's your body changes.
sentences.zh: 你的身体在改变。

sentences.en: It's your feeling about others change.
sentences.zh: 你对他人的感受在改变。

sentences.en: It's your feeling about your authority in the world changes.
sentences.zh: 你对自己在这个世界上权威感的认知也在改变。

sentences.en: How do you reflect that with your clothing?
sentences.zh: 你如何通过服装来反映这一点？

sentences.en: That gets at the very most difficult question about fashion, period.
sentences.zh: 这触及了时尚界最困难的问题。

sentences.en: So, it's not surprising to me that so many readers would ask, like, how do I dress my age?
sentences.zh: 所以，我不奇怪为什么这么多读者会问：我该如何穿出符合年龄的风格？

sentences.en: Because how do I talk my age?
sentences.zh: 因为我该如何谈吐得体？

sentences.en: How do I feel my age?
sentences.zh: 我该如何感受自己的年龄？

sentences.en: You know, I might feel a lot younger than I seem or that I look.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我可能感觉比我看起来要年轻得多。

sentences.en: So, I would say it's probably okay for him to dress like he did when he was 20, as long as it's okay for him socially.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想说，只要在社交场合没问题，他穿得像20岁时那样可能也没关系。

sentences.en: But if it doesn't line up with how he feels as a person, he's going to have to actually spend some time thinking about how he feels as a person.
sentences.zh: 但如果这与他作为个人的感受不符，他就必须花点时间思考一下他作为个人的感受。

sentences.en: And then he'll figure out how to dress.
sentences.zh: 然后他就会知道该怎么穿了。

sentences.en: I think we think that clothes will answer those questions for us.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们以为衣服能帮我们回答这些问题。

sentences.en: But, in fact, we have to answer those questions and then go out and find the clothes that match our feelings about ourselves.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，我们必须先回答这些问题，然后去寻找与我们自我感受相匹配的衣服。

sentences.en: And, you know, that actually evolves fairly frequently as we age.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，随着年龄增长，这种感受实际上会经常演变。

sentences.en: And that's why you're getting questions from people in their 80s, 70s, 60s, and lower is that, like, we're always trying to navigate this problem.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你会收到80多岁、70多岁、60多岁以及更年轻的人的提问，因为我们一直在试图解决这个问题。

sentences.en: Well, I think a lot of people don't want to, again, dress like they're trying to be 25 when they're in their 40s.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为很多人不想在40多岁时还刻意打扮得像25岁。

sentences.en: Or they don't want to try too hard to look cool even though they want to feel good in their clothing.
sentences.zh: 或者他们不想为了看起来很酷而用力过猛，尽管他们确实想在穿衣时感觉良好。

sentences.en: One thing that I keep saying and thinking is that it is almost impossible to escape the moment in which you were forged.
sentences.zh: 我一直说并思考的一点是，你几乎无法逃脱你所处的时代对你的塑造。

sentences.en: You cannot quite shake that.
sentences.zh: 你无法完全摆脱这一点。

sentences.en: Whether you're a boomer, whether you're a, you know, Gen X, whether you're a Gen Z, like, it just will be there.
sentences.zh: 无论你是婴儿潮一代、X世代还是Z世代，它都会在那里。

sentences.en: And there's something in there that you can't quite fight.
sentences.zh: 其中有些东西是你无法抗拒的。

sentences.en: And that's okay.
sentences.zh: 这没关系。

sentences.en: Stella, I went to a Catholic all-boys high school and I still dress that way.
sentences.zh: Stella，我上的是天主教全男校，我至今还是那样穿。

sentences.en: I think I locked it in when I was 16 years old.
sentences.zh: 我想我在16岁时就把这种风格定型了。

sentences.en: So, that was a really beautiful answer.
sentences.zh: 那真是一个非常精彩的回答。

sentences.en: I thought that was really eloquent.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那非常有说服力。

sentences.en: You're going to tell me I'm wrong.
sentences.zh: 你是不是要说我错了？

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: I think that you are absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我认为你是完全正确的。

sentences.en: But I'm trying to think of how materially to help here.
sentences.zh: 但我正在思考如何在实质上提供帮助。

sentences.en: And what I would say is already asking the question clearly indicates that there's something that when Paul and people like Paul look in the mirror,
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，提出这个问题本身就清楚地表明，当Paul和像Paul这样的人照镜子时，

sentences.en: they think, I'm dissatisfied with this.
sentences.zh: 他们会想：我对现在的样子不满意。

sentences.en: This seems off of who I am or who I'm trying to be.
sentences.zh: 这似乎与我是谁或我想成为谁不符。

sentences.en: And what I would say is try to then stand there and figure out maybe what part of what you're wearing makes you feel that the most and begin there.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，试着站在镜子前，找出你身上哪部分让你感觉最不舒服，然后从那里开始。

sentences.en: Like, if it is that you're still wearing the same exact chinos you wore in high school or the same exact sort of Catholic school button-up, if you will,
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你穿的还是高中时那条一模一样的斜纹棉布裤，或者那件天主教学校的衬衫，

sentences.en: and that that is pulling you too far backwards or too far to that time that you want to pull out of,
sentences.zh: 而这把你拉得太远，回到了那个你想摆脱的时期，

sentences.en: then begin there and start slowly and try to figure out how you might update or even just modify that a little bit within your box.
sentences.zh: 那就从那里开始，慢慢尝试，看看如何在你的框架内更新甚至只是稍微修改一下它。

sentences.en: Don't go out and buy seven gajillion patterned shirts because you've worn solid shirts your whole life.
sentences.zh: 不要因为你一辈子都穿纯色衬衫，就跑去买几万件花衬衫。

sentences.en: That's just a waste of money and you will not actually end up wearing those.
sentences.zh: 那只是浪费钱，而且你最终根本不会穿它们。

sentences.en: I'd say zero in on that thing and then build outward from there.
sentences.zh: 我会说锁定那个点，然后从那里向外扩展。

sentences.en: That would – and don't get daunted by that process.
sentences.zh: 这会——而且不要被这个过程吓倒。

sentences.en: That would be my guidance.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的建议。

sentences.en: That is very actionable advice.
sentences.zh: 那是非常可行的建议。

sentences.en: That's good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Like, start with the shoes, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如，从鞋子开始。

sentences.en: Or, you know, start with something that you –
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，从一些你——

sentences.en: Oh, my shoes are so hard.
sentences.zh: 哦，鞋子太难了。

sentences.en: Yeah, but you can – most people, let's say, your weight changes as you age or your – you know, you go through surgeries or, you know, you have all kinds of physical changes.
sentences.zh: 是的，但是你可以——大多数人，比如说，你的体重会随着年龄增长而改变，或者你经历过手术，或者你有各种各样的身体变化。

sentences.en: But shoes can be one way that a person can update their look quickly, that, you know, they come in a different range of prices.
sentences.zh: 但鞋子可以是人们快速更新外观的一种方式，而且它们有不同的价格区间。

sentences.en: You're probably not going to outgrow them.
sentences.zh: 你可能不会穿不下它们。

sentences.en: They are – you know, if you wanted to make a big investment, you could justify that because you'll wear them all the time and you'll get them repaired.
sentences.zh: 它们是——你知道，如果你想进行大额投资，你可以证明这是合理的，因为你会一直穿它们，并且可以拿去维修。

sentences.en: Like, that's a good place to start.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的切入点。

sentences.en: I feel like this is related to our next question, which is from Laura in Menlo Park, California.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这和我们的下一个问题有关，来自加州门洛帕克的Laura。

sentences.en: Laura writes that after giving birth to her son, none of her clothes felt appropriate to wear anymore.
sentences.zh: Laura写道，在生下儿子后，她觉得以前的衣服都不适合穿了。

sentences.en: And again, touching on this theme we've been talking about, the clothes that she accumulated in her 20s no longer matched her sense of self.
sentences.zh: 再次触及我们一直在讨论的主题，她在20多岁时积累的衣服不再符合她的自我认知。

sentences.en: She's a different person now inherently as a new parent.
sentences.zh: 作为一名新手妈妈，她本质上已经是一个不同的人了。

sentences.en: So, she asks, quote, how do you suggest navigating this early motherhood era with regard to personal style?
sentences.zh: 所以她问：“你建议如何处理这个新手妈妈阶段的个人风格？”

sentences.en: And how do you do so without going broke?
sentences.zh: 而且如何在不破产的情况下做到这一点？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I would say the transition to new motherhood is one of the most profound shifts a woman is going to experience in her life, in her body, you know, in relation to others,
sentences.zh: 我想说，向新手妈妈的转变是一个女人一生中经历的最深刻的转变之一，无论是身体上，还是与他人的关系上，

sentences.en: in relation to the child she now has to take care of.
sentences.zh: 以及与她现在必须照顾的孩子之间的关系上。

sentences.en: So, you're also navigating a realignment to who you feel you are in the world.
sentences.zh: 所以，你也在经历一场关于“你觉得自己在世界上是谁”的重新定位。

sentences.en: That's maybe the most difficult of all that I've experienced and that I've witnessed other people experience.
sentences.zh: 这可能是我经历过以及见证过别人经历过的最困难的事情。

sentences.en: And similar to our other answer, I think it's got to happen gradually if you can't afford to just throw it all out and start over,
sentences.zh: 和我们之前的回答类似，如果你负担不起全部扔掉重来，我认为必须循序渐进，

sentences.en: which is this sort of fantasy I don't think anybody can really, you know, unless you're a very rich celebrity,
sentences.zh: 这是一种幻想，我不认为任何人真的能做到，除非你是非常有钱的名人，

sentences.en: chances are you're going to have a lot of the same old stuff you always had.
sentences.zh: 否则你很可能还是会保留很多以前的老东西。

sentences.en: How to make it work.
sentences.zh: 如何让它们发挥作用。

sentences.en: I guess, not to be corny, but to be slightly gentle with yourself as you go through that.
sentences.zh: 我想，不是要说套话，而是要在这个过程中对自己稍微温柔一点。

sentences.en: Maybe pick up one or two things that you feel really good in.
sentences.zh: 也许买一两件让你感觉真正好的东西。

sentences.en: It's kind of the opposite of what Jacob is saying is, like, identify the thing that makes you feel the worSt.
sentences.zh: 这和Jacob说的正好相反，他是说找出让你感觉最糟糕的东西。

sentences.en: But this would be, like, go out and treat yourself to at least one thing that you do really feel good in that does express that about you.
sentences.zh: 但我的建议是，去买至少一件让你感觉真正好、并且能表达出你个性的东西。

sentences.en: You start with that and then wear it to death.
sentences.zh: 从那件开始，然后把它穿到旧。

sentences.en: Kind of just wear it all the time.
sentences.zh: 就一直穿它。

sentences.en: That's what I would say.
sentences.zh: 这就是我想说的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, I'm a man, so my answer will be very gendered in this way.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然我是个男人，所以我的回答会有很强的性别色彩。

sentences.en: But I'm a new father.
sentences.zh: 但我是一位新手父亲。

sentences.en: My son is less than five months old, as we speak.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，我儿子还不到五个月大。

sentences.en: And I truly just got off leave like a week ago.
sentences.zh: 我确实是一周前才刚结束休假。

sentences.en: And I went through that entire period of leave dressing in almost the exact same thing every single day.
sentences.zh: 在那段休假期间，我几乎每天都穿着完全一样的东西。

sentences.en: I wore shorts and an old shirt, like an old tee, every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都穿短裤和一件旧衬衫，就像那种旧T恤一样。

sentences.en: And I did that for months.
sentences.zh: 我这样坚持了好几个月。

sentences.en: And I was fine.
sentences.zh: 而且我感觉还不错。

sentences.en: You know, obviously, you're so sleep-deprived and you're so whatever.
sentences.zh: 你知道，显然，你当时极度缺觉，整个人状态很差。

sentences.en: Like, you're not seeing people.
sentences.zh: 比如，你根本见不到什么人。

sentences.en: You're like, who cares?
sentences.zh: 你会觉得，谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: Just get me dressed so I can have, you know, feed him.
sentences.zh: 只要能穿上衣服，让我能去喂他就行了。

sentences.en: And I think it took until, like, two weeks before I came back to work.
sentences.zh: 我想直到我重返工作岗位前两周，我才终于做了点改变。

sentences.en: I went and I did buy something.
sentences.zh: 我确实去买了一些东西。

sentences.en: And I bought something that was, like, very personal to it.
sentences.zh: 而且我买的东西，怎么说呢，非常有个人特色。

sentences.en: Like, it was very, like, of my style, quote-unquote.
sentences.zh: 就是那种，用所谓的“我的风格”来形容吧。

sentences.en: It was a sweater.
sentences.zh: 那是一件毛衣。

sentences.en: It, like, had—
sentences.zh: 它，怎么说呢——

sentences.en: It's not this sweater.
sentences.zh: 不是这件毛衣。

sentences.en: No, it's not this sweater.
sentences.zh: 不，不是这件。

sentences.en: It had, like, a funky pattern to it.
sentences.zh: 它有一种很时髦的图案。

sentences.en: And it felt like I was, like, oh, this is a reminder of, like, what I like and who I am.
sentences.zh: 当时感觉就像是，哦，这提醒了我，我喜欢什么，我是谁。

sentences.en: Because it is really difficult.
sentences.zh: 因为这真的很难。

sentences.en: Like, you're—like, I think I look at a lot of stuff in my drawer right now and it feels very juvenile, which makes, like, no sense because I only wore that, like, a year ago.
sentences.zh: 比如，我觉得我现在看着抽屉里的很多东西，都觉得太幼稚了，这完全没道理，因为我一年前才穿过它们。

sentences.en: But then there's other things where I'm, like, does this make me look too much like a dad?
sentences.zh: 但还有些东西，我会想，这会不会让我看起来太像个老爸了？

sentences.en: Like, what is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: And then what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那又意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: And you're just kind of tortured by it a little bit.
sentences.zh: 你会被这些念头折磨得有点心烦意乱。

sentences.en: But I think that's a great piece of advice, Stella.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这是一个很好的建议，Stella。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: This one, I'm actually—I'm interested in this one.
sentences.zh: 这个，我其实——我对这个很感兴趣。

sentences.en: As a dude who sees dudes dressing terribly.
sentences.zh: 作为一个经常看到男士穿得一塌糊涂的男人。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So this is from Kale in New Haven, Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 这是来自康涅狄格州纽黑文市的Kale。

sentences.en: Don't know where he went to college.
sentences.zh: 不知道他大学在哪读的。

sentences.en: He is a law student who describes himself as, quote, never particularly concerned about fashion or style.
sentences.zh: 他是一名法学院学生，他自称“从来不太关心时尚或风格”。

sentences.en: But he gets anxious about making sure his outfit fits the particular setting he's in.
sentences.zh: 但他会因为担心自己的着装是否符合特定场合而感到焦虑。

sentences.en: So he asks, what are good rules of thumb I can or should be following to make sure I'm not finding myself chronically overdressed or underdressed?
sentences.zh: 所以他问，我能或应该遵循哪些好的经验法则，以确保自己不会总是穿得过于正式或过于随意？

sentences.en: And this touches on a theme that a lot of, I think, men asked about, which is how do they dress better than they do now without looking overly formal?
sentences.zh: 这触及了一个我认为很多男性都问过的主题，那就是如何在不显得过于正式的情况下，比现在穿得更好？

sentences.en: I would say that what I've observed is that many men, their primary goal—I'm going to be grossly generalist—is not to stand out too much.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，据我观察，许多男性的首要目标——我在这里进行一个粗略的概括——就是不要太引人注目。

sentences.en: And that's, you know, there are all kinds of social reasons for that that are above my pay grade, but, you know, are quite deep and psychological.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这背后有各种各样的社会原因，超出了我的理解范围，但它们相当深刻且具有心理学意义。

sentences.en: So, you know, I don't know—you know about red sock theory?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我不知道——你知道“红袜理论”吗？

sentences.en: Do you know about that?
sentences.zh: 你知道那个吗？

sentences.en: Oh, God, please tell me about this.
sentences.zh: 天哪，请一定要告诉我。

sentences.en: No, go ahead.
sentences.zh: 不，你先说。

sentences.en: No, you go ahead.
sentences.zh: 不，你先说。

sentences.en: No, you go ahead.
sentences.zh: 不，你先说。

sentences.en: Well, I might mingle it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我可能会把它讲得乱七八糟。

sentences.en: But what I understand it to be is that you can pick one item to have a little bit of flair and that people will respond well to that tiny bit of flair.
sentences.zh: 但我理解的意思是，你可以选择一件单品来增加一点点风采，人们会对那一点点风采做出很好的回应。

sentences.en: But if you, let's say, put a red blazer on, they might not respond as well.
sentences.zh: 但如果你，比如说，穿了一件红色的西装外套，他们的反应可能就不会那么好了。

sentences.en: You're standing out too much, so you want to stand out just a little but not too much.
sentences.zh: 你太引人注目了，所以你想稍微突出一点，但又不能太过分。

sentences.en: And that's what red sock theory comes from.
sentences.zh: 这就是“红袜理论”的由来。

sentences.en: But I do feel like maybe this person asking this question wants a little bit of flair, but not too much.
sentences.zh: 但我确实觉得，也许这个提问的人想要一点点风采，但又不想太多。

sentences.en: Like, they want to walk a line, but not—why are you giving me that?
sentences.zh: 就像，他们想走一条中间路线，但不是——你为什么要那样看着我？

sentences.en: Because I have several pairs of red socks.
sentences.zh: 因为我有好几双红袜子。

sentences.en: That's why.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Well, you're special.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你很特别。

sentences.en: Oh, God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: I was going to say, the unfortunate thing about the red sock theory is that a lot of people know it, so a lot of people do the same trick, so it doesn't become as memorable.
sentences.zh: 我本来想说，关于红袜理论不幸的一点是，很多人都知道它，所以很多人都在用同样的招数，它就不那么令人印象深刻了。

sentences.en: I actually think—I'm, like, wondering, as I sit here, I think this guy should go the other way.
sentences.zh: 我其实认为——我坐在这里就在想，我觉得这家伙应该反其道而行之。

sentences.en: I mean, I feel this is like— You mean he should go formal?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我觉得这就像是——你是说他应该穿得正式点？

sentences.en: I think he should just wear a suit all the time.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他应该一直穿西装。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, that's a good option.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是个不错的选择。

sentences.en: Better to be overdressed.
sentences.zh: 穿得正式点总比穿得随意好。

sentences.en: I think it's like, if I'm this guy and I'm thinking, I'm concerned about being overdressed, people will very—unless you're wearing a tuxedo,
sentences.zh: 我觉得，如果我是这家伙，我在想，我担心穿得太正式，人们会非常——除非你穿的是燕尾服，

sentences.en: they will very rarely judge you for being overdressed.
sentences.zh: 否则他们很少会因为你穿得太正式而评判你。

sentences.en: I think you might feel a bit abnormal in that immediate moment, but you're not going to be judged.
sentences.zh: 我想你当时可能会觉得有点不自在，但你不会被评判。

sentences.en: And to the red sock theory, you will probably be remembered.
sentences.zh: 而且根据红袜理论，你很可能会被人记住。

sentences.en: And especially in this universe where I think people—men in particular—sit in this kind of weird, wishy-washy zone of business casual, sometimes too business, sometimes too casual,
sentences.zh: 特别是在这个宇宙中，我认为人们——尤其是男性——处于一种奇怪的、模棱两可的商务休闲地带，有时太商务，有时太休闲，

sentences.en: whatever.
sentences.zh: 随便吧。

sentences.en: It's like just—I think you could lean in, wear the suit, wear a tie even.
sentences.zh: 就像是——我觉得你可以坚持下去，穿上西装，甚至打上领带。

sentences.en: I'd say not vary it up that much if you're going to do that.
sentences.zh: 如果非要这样做的话，我建议不要有太大的变化。

sentences.en: I'd say keep it pretty, you know, standard suit, maybe solid-colored knit tie, solid-colored shirt.
sentences.zh: 我建议保持相当标准，你知道，标准的西装，也许是纯色的针织领带，纯色的衬衫。

sentences.en: But, like, get a good template going, and maybe that's just what you wear all the time.
sentences.zh: 但是，找一个好的模板，也许这就是你一直穿的风格。

sentences.en: And you can lean into that if you're comfortable with it.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得舒服，你可以坚持下去。

sentences.en: I'd say otherwise, you know, it's tough because I think, yeah, I think too many men are in that kind of muddy middle right now where it's like, oh,
sentences.zh: 否则的话，你知道，这很难，因为我觉得，是的，我觉得现在太多的男人处于那种模糊的中间地带，就像，哦，

sentences.en: here's my button-up shirt with my, like, V-neck sweater over and—or my performance polo.
sentences.zh: 这是我的扣领衬衫，外面套着V领毛衣，或者我的功能性Polo衫。

sentences.en: And, you know, then you just look kind of pedestrian.
sentences.zh: 然后，你就看起来很平庸。

sentences.en: Yeah, a lot of half-sips.
sentences.zh: 是的，很多半吊子的穿搭。

sentences.en: Yeah, a lot of—I think the half-measure—
sentences.zh: 是的，很多——我认为这种半吊子的做法——

sentences.en: Quarter, quarters.
sentences.zh: 四分之一，四分之一。

sentences.en: The half-measure is where you're in trouble, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为半吊子的做法才是问题的所在。

sentences.en: I like what you're saying, which is basically, like, be bold.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢你说的，基本上就是，要大胆。

sentences.en: Go for it.
sentences.zh: 去做吧。

sentences.en: Go for it.
sentences.zh: 去做吧。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Can we touch on the obvious, which is did the pandemic break the way some people think about clothing?
sentences.zh: 我们能谈谈显而易见的事情吗，就是疫情是否改变了人们对服装的看法？

sentences.en: Oh, a thousand percent.
sentences.zh: 哦，百分之一千改变了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's like—I wonder if she's going to disagree, but I think, like—
sentences.zh: 就像——我想知道她是否会不同意，但我认为，就像——

sentences.en: Well, it didn't change me in any way.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它对我没有任何改变。

sentences.en: Well, I think—
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想——

sentences.en: Okay, we got it, Stella.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们知道了，Stella。

sentences.en: I think it—I think it irreparably changed what the market for clothes is.
sentences.zh: 我认为它——我认为它不可逆转地改变了服装市场。

sentences.en: You know, I think we were maybe heading in a different direction before the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我觉得在疫情之前，我们可能正朝着不同的方向发展。

sentences.en: Like, you know, this is such a very specific high-fashion example, but I remember being at a Louis Vuitton show just before the pandemic happened, and there were a lot of suits.
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道，这是一个非常具体的时尚例子，但我记得在疫情发生前不久，我参加了一场路易威登的时装秀，那里有很多西装。

sentences.en: And I thought, okay, this is something that people are going to try to message around.
sentences.zh: 我想，好吧，这是人们会尝试去传达的东西。

sentences.en: This is what the brand's going to try to package.
sentences.zh: 这是品牌会尝试包装的东西。

sentences.en: This is what magazines might try to make editorials out of.
sentences.zh: 这是杂志可能会尝试制作社论的东西。

sentences.en: This is going to be a talking point, and then, boom, the pandemic happened.
sentences.zh: 这本来会成为一个谈资，然后，砰，疫情发生了。

sentences.en: Those clothes hit the stores, but they, you know, did in a very muted way because of when they landed.
sentences.zh: 那些衣服进入了商店，但它们，你知道，因为上市的时间，表现得非常低调。

sentences.en: People were at home in sweatpants.
sentences.zh: 人们都在家里穿着运动裤。

sentences.en: I think that the casualization of everything, it's like you can't put that back in the box, you know?
sentences.zh: 我认为一切的休闲化，就像你无法把它放回盒子里一样，你知道吗？

sentences.en: You can't put the toothpaste back in the tube.
sentences.zh: 你无法把挤出来的牙膏再装回管子里。

sentences.en: I think people still do, in a lot of ways, shop with how can I feel comfortable as the number one criteria and often, I think, the only criteria.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们在很多方面仍然以“我如何感到舒适”作为第一标准，而且我认为通常也是唯一的标准。

sentences.en: I think pulling back a little bit is like what it did to our whole society where we became disaggregated and a little siloed.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种退缩有点像它对我们整个社会所做的事情，我们变得分散且有点孤立。

sentences.en: That will have a profound effect on the ability for trends to kind of take hold because you can live in your little echo chamber where, you know,
sentences.zh: 这将对趋势产生深远的影响，因为你可以生活在自己的小回声室里，在那里，你知道，

sentences.en: boat shoes are cool and never have to confront a group of people that think they're not cool.
sentences.zh: 船鞋很酷，而且永远不必面对一群认为它们不酷的人。

sentences.en: And so, to the extent that the pandemic just further atomized us, yes, I think it has been profound.
sentences.zh: 所以，就疫情进一步将我们原子化而言，是的，我认为影响是深远的。

sentences.en: So, this is good.
sentences.zh: 所以，这很好。

sentences.en: This is good because Maggie from Summit, New Jersey, she has a question that relates to what you're talking about here, I think.
sentences.zh: 这很好，因为来自新泽西州萨米特的Maggie，她有一个问题，我认为与你在这里谈论的内容有关。

sentences.en: She says she's really concerned with coming off as, quote, a trend hopper.
sentences.zh: 她说她非常担心被视为“潮流追随者”。

sentences.en: She says that she finds that whenever she goes back to something in her closet, it inevitably feels like she's drafting off what other people are wearing,
sentences.zh: 她说她发现每当她回到衣柜里找东西时，感觉就像是在模仿别人穿的东西，

sentences.en: even though it's just her wardrobe.
sentences.zh: 尽管那只是她自己的衣橱。

sentences.en: So, she writes, I feel like it's harder than ever to curate a unique personal style without parts or the whole becoming social media's latest microtrend.
sentences.zh: 所以她写道，我觉得比以往任何时候都更难策划出独特的个人风格，而不让部分或整体成为社交媒体最新的微趋势。

sentences.en: I guess she's worried about appearing trendy to the world, if I'm understanding this correctly.
sentences.zh: 我想她是在担心在世界上显得太赶时髦，如果我理解正确的话。

sentences.en: So, what would either of you say to Maggie?
sentences.zh: 那么，你们两位会对Maggie说什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think Maggie just needs to be okay with her wearing the thing.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得Maggie只需要对自己穿的东西感到自在就行了。

sentences.en: Like, don't worry about how people are going to perceive you in it.
sentences.zh: 比如，不要担心别人会怎么看你。

sentences.en: I think also, as we've discussed, like, everything feels like a trend all the time.
sentences.zh: 我也认为，正如我们讨论过的，一切似乎一直都是潮流。

sentences.en: You know, shirts are long, shirts are short, like, pants are wide, pants are narrow.
sentences.zh: 你知道，衬衫变长了，衬衫变短了，裤子变宽了，裤子变窄了。

sentences.en: Like, everything is possible.
sentences.zh: 一切皆有可能。

sentences.en: And so, within that, it's like, tune out that noise.
sentences.zh: 所以，在那种情况下，就像，屏蔽掉那些噪音。

sentences.en: Just, if there's something in your closet you want to wear, just wear it.
sentences.zh: 如果你的衣柜里有你想穿的东西，就穿它。

sentences.en: If you want to buy the thing, you're never going to be able to identify how you were incepted to buy the thing.
sentences.zh: 如果你想买那件东西，你永远无法确定你是如何被诱导去买它的。

sentences.en: You know, like, you're in a store, you see something that's yellow, you might like it, without realizing that butter yellow was the trend of last year or what have you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像，你在店里，看到黄色的东西，你可能会喜欢它，而没有意识到奶油黄是去年的流行趋势之类的。

sentences.en: If you are personally compelled toward something, don't waste your time psychoanalyzing why you're compelled toward it.
sentences.zh: 如果你个人被某样东西吸引，不要浪费时间去分析为什么会被它吸引。

sentences.en: If you like it, it makes you happy, you think you'll look good in it, just wear it.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢它，它让你快乐，你觉得你穿上它很好看，那就穿吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, you just pulled a Miranda Priestly right there.
sentences.zh: 是的，你刚才就像Miranda Priestly一样。

sentences.en: You're like, that butter yellow that you're wearing?
sentences.zh: 你就像是，你穿的那件奶油黄？

sentences.en: You may not know how it got into the store.
sentences.zh: 你可能不知道它是怎么进入商店的。

sentences.en: I think color is still where that does, where the trickle down is still probably the most potent.
sentences.zh: 我认为颜色仍然是那种渗透力最强的地方。

sentences.en: But, yeah.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的。

sentences.en: I have a question that is going to draft off a little bit of what you were talking about here.
sentences.zh: 我有一个问题，会延续一点你刚才谈论的内容。

sentences.en: This is Dana, Tempe, Arizona.
sentences.zh: 这是亚利桑那州坦佩市的Dana。

sentences.en: Dana asks, quote, how can you keep up with trends while trying to limit overconsumption and make environmentally conscious style choices?
sentences.zh: Dana问，“如何在限制过度消费和做出环保风格选择的同时跟上潮流？”

sentences.en: You cannot.
sentences.zh: 你做不到。

sentences.en: You actually cannot.
sentences.zh: 你实际上做不到。

sentences.en: There's no ethical consumption under capitalism?
sentences.zh: 资本主义下没有道德消费？

sentences.en: Well, you can buy vintage clothing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可以买复古服装。

sentences.en: That is a choice that you can make.
sentences.zh: 那是一个你可以做出的选择。

sentences.en: My personal mission would be to tell people to stop following trends in that way and to think more about what they like and to wear what they like.
sentences.zh: 我个人的使命是告诉人们停止那样追随潮流，多思考他们喜欢什么，穿他们喜欢的衣服。

sentences.en: But I'm anti-trend.
sentences.zh: 但我反潮流。

sentences.en: Why are you posing to me like I'm pro-trend?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要把我表现得好像我是支持潮流的？

sentences.en: I feel like you're about to argue with me.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你正要和我争论。

sentences.en: Can you just, before you respond, what is anti-trend?
sentences.zh: 在你回答之前，你能告诉我什么是反潮流吗？

sentences.en: What does that mean for the styles?
sentences.zh: 这对风格意味着什么？

sentences.en: I don't think that people should change how they look and dress and act every six months.
sentences.zh: 我不认为人们应该每六个月就改变他们的外表、穿着和行为。

sentences.en: I fundamentally think that that has been a problem with the fashion industry.
sentences.zh: 我从根本上认为这是时尚界的一个问题。

sentences.en: I think you should not even encourage people to do that.
sentences.zh: 我认为你不应该鼓励人们这样做。

sentences.en: There's something grossly consumerist and unsustainable about that behavior.
sentences.zh: 这种行为有一种极其消费主义且不可持续的成分。

sentences.en: You know, one thing that we haven't touched on here is the way in which trends often have to do with silhouette and proportionality of clothing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在这里没有触及的一点是，潮流往往与服装的轮廓和比例有关。

sentences.en: And so, you know, the ways that something might look five years ago or ten years ago have to do with, like, how high your hemline is, how short your shirt is.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，五年前或十年前看起来的样子，与你的下摆有多高、衬衫有多短有关。

sentences.en: You know, Jacob has a piece coming out this week about men's shirts getting shorter and shorter and shorter.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，Jacob这周要发一篇文章，讲的是男士衬衫变得越来越短。

sentences.en: Not crop tops, but just sort of regular button-up shirts and how they now have a kind of a flat front.
sentences.zh: 不是露脐装，就是那种普通的扣子衬衫，讲它们现在怎么都变成了平前襟的设计。

sentences.en: And then I have Gen Z children who shop in thrift stores and, you know, they sew their clothes to look like that because they can't afford brand new clothes.
sentences.zh: 我那些Z世代的孩子们会在二手店买衣服，你知道的，他们会自己缝改衣服，让它们看起来像那样，因为他们买不起全新的衣服。

sentences.en: And it's more sustainable and they're into that.
sentences.zh: 而且这样更可持续，他们很喜欢这一点。

sentences.en: So, paying attention to the ways that designers are suggesting that you wear your clothes enables you to keep up with the trends in a variety of ways.
sentences.zh: 所以，关注设计师建议的穿搭方式，能让你以各种方式紧跟潮流。

sentences.en: Like, you could buy an old shirt and chop it up and make it look like the silhouette of the quote-unquote moment.
sentences.zh: 比如，你可以买一件旧衬衫，把它剪短，做出那种所谓的“当季”廓形。

sentences.en: And that's a sustainable way to quote-unquote keep up with trends.
sentences.zh: 这是一种所谓的“紧跟潮流”的可持续方式。

sentences.en: It's also just kind of a fun, like, in the sporting mode of what are people wearing.
sentences.zh: 这也算是一种乐趣，就像是在观察人们都在穿什么一样。

sentences.en: It's just one way that you can start to think about clothes.
sentences.zh: 这只是你可以开始思考服装的一种方式。

sentences.en: And I think the idea of silhouette, that's actually a big part of what we're talking about when we talk about trends.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为廓形这个概念，其实是我们谈论潮流时很大的一部分。

sentences.en: Yeah, I do agree with Stella.
sentences.zh: 是的，我同意Stella的看法。

sentences.en: I think, you know, people want to say vintage is sustainable.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，你知道，人们总想说复古就是可持续的。

sentences.en: I don't really buy that 100% because I think the way vintage is treated now, it's still treated as, like, a very consumption-based habit.
sentences.zh: 我并不完全买账，因为我觉得现在对待复古的方式，依然是一种非常基于消费的习惯。

sentences.en: It's still more sustainable.
sentences.zh: 它确实还是更可持续一些。

sentences.en: It's certainly still more sustainable.
sentences.zh: 当然，它确实还是更可持续。

sentences.en: I don't want to, like, cut into that.
sentences.zh: 我不想否定这一点。

sentences.en: But, like, you know, our habit remains, like, consumption-based.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我们的习惯依然是基于消费的。

sentences.en: Like, we still want to buy the hot new thing and feel like we're kind of taking part within fashion.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们还是想买最火的新品，感觉自己参与到了时尚之中。

sentences.en: And to be truly sustainable within that is very, very, very difficult.
sentences.zh: 要在这种情况下做到真正的可持续，是非常、非常、非常困难的。

sentences.en: And I also think it's worth noting that, like, you know, vintage clothes are not, you know, always better made.
sentences.zh: 而且我还觉得值得注意的是，你知道，复古服装并不总是质量更好。

sentences.en: You know, especially now as we get closer and closer to things from the 2000s being considered vintage.
sentences.zh: 你知道，尤其是现在，我们越来越接近把2000年代的东西也视为复古了。

sentences.en: Like, they're probably just as, you know, fast fashion disposable as a lot of stuff that's in stores.
sentences.zh: 它们可能和店里卖的很多东西一样，都是快时尚的一次性产品。

sentences.en: And we're kind of heading toward a weird time in the vintage market for that reason.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，我们正走向复古市场一个奇怪的时期。

sentences.en: But, yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 不过，确实，没错。

sentences.en: It goes back to kind of what I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 这又回到了我刚才说的观点。

sentences.en: It's just like, and also what you're saying, buy one thing.
sentences.zh: 就像，还有你说的，买一件东西就好。

sentences.en: Buy one thing.
sentences.zh: 买一件东西。

sentences.en: Buy one thing.
sentences.zh: 买一件东西。

sentences.en: That's what I was going to come back to.
sentences.zh: 我正想回到这一点。

sentences.en: Buy one thing.
sentences.zh: 买一件东西。

sentences.en: That's a way that you can be more.
sentences.zh: 这就是你可以做得更多的方式。

sentences.en: And wear that thing all the time.
sentences.zh: 然后一直穿那件东西。

sentences.en: Wear it a lot.
sentences.zh: 多穿穿它。

sentences.en: Wear it until you're sick of it and you can buy your next one thing.
sentences.zh: 穿到你厌倦了为止，然后再买下一件东西。

sentences.en: And that instead of, you know, a lot of us grew up with this idea that, like, it's back to school,
sentences.zh: 而不是像我们很多人从小被灌输的那样，觉得开学了，

sentences.en: so you're going to get a new bunch of clothes and you're going to change who you are every year.
sentences.zh: 所以你要买一堆新衣服，每年都要换个样子。

sentences.en: And, you know, I don't know if that's the Sears catalog of my childhood, you know, Pavlovian experience that it's September, so I feel like I have to reinvent myself.
sentences.zh: 而且，我不知道这是否是我童年时西尔斯百货目录带来的巴甫洛夫式体验，觉得到了九月，我就必须重塑自我。

sentences.en: Well, I just went through this, you know, new pair of sneakers, new pair of, you know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我刚经历过这个，你知道，新运动鞋，新的一套，你知道的。

sentences.en: Yeah, but actually breaking free from that idea and, you know, I do think that the pandemic,
sentences.zh: 是的，但实际上摆脱那种想法，而且，我确实认为疫情期间，

sentences.en: the one way in which it really did actually change the way I dress is that I was wearing the same thing over and over and over again and it felt great.
sentences.zh: 它确实改变了我穿衣方式的一点就是，我一直在穿同一件衣服，感觉棒极了。

sentences.en: And when I'd go out, I'd wear the same coat to every event and that was fine.
sentences.zh: 当我出门时，我参加每个活动都穿同一件外套，那也很好。

sentences.en: I didn't need a new dress.
sentences.zh: 我不需要新裙子。

sentences.en: I didn't need, you know, to habituate myself to novelty.
sentences.zh: 我不需要让自己习惯于追求新鲜感。

sentences.en: And that is actually at the answer of almost every one of these questions.
sentences.zh: 而这其实就是几乎所有这些问题的答案。

sentences.en: It's like if you feel like you're not yourself, pick one way in which you want to alter it.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得不像你自己了，选一个你想改变的地方去改就好。

sentences.en: If you want to be sustainable, buy less, pick one thing and wear it all the time.
sentences.zh: 如果你想可持续，就少买点，选一件东西一直穿。

sentences.en: If you want to be fashionable like everybody else, like pick the one thing that you think is holding you back and alter that.
sentences.zh: 如果你想和别人一样时髦，就选出那个你觉得拖你后腿的东西，然后改掉它。

sentences.en: This is a really good advice.
sentences.zh: 这建议真的很好。

sentences.en: Our final reader question is specifically for Jacob.
sentences.zh: 我们最后一位读者的提问是专门给Jacob的。

sentences.en: It is a reader named Schmilbert Schmooze from New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 是一位来自新泽西州的读者，名叫Schmilbert Schmooze。

sentences.en: He wants to know, Jacob, should he be wearing double pleated trousers?
sentences.zh: 他想问，Jacob，他应该穿双褶长裤吗？

sentences.en: All he has are flat front pants.
sentences.zh: 他只有平前襟的裤子。

sentences.en: Okay, I do think you should try double pleated trousers.
sentences.zh: 好的，我确实认为你应该试试双褶长裤。

sentences.en: Yeah, why?
sentences.zh: 是吗，为什么？

sentences.en: So I only buy pants that have two pleats, pretty much.
sentences.zh: 我基本上只买有双褶的裤子。

sentences.en: I think maybe these are, no, these are one pleat today.
sentences.zh: 我想也许这些是，不，今天这些是单褶的。

sentences.en: But these are also very, very wide through the leg that I'm wearing.
sentences.zh: 但我穿的这条裤子裤腿也非常、非常宽。

sentences.en: I think they are more comfortable.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它们更舒服。

sentences.en: I will advocate for that.
sentences.zh: 我会支持这一点。

sentences.en: I think they are more comfortable and I think that it is a very, the comfort side, I think it's a very good way to add intrigue.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它们更舒服，而且我认为，从舒适的角度来看，这是增加趣味性的一种很好的方式。

sentences.en: Because it modifies one part of your outfit and everything else can remain balanced up top.
sentences.zh: 因为它只改变了你装束的一部分，而上半身的其他部分可以保持平衡。

sentences.en: Everything can remain the same.
sentences.zh: 一切都可以保持不变。

sentences.en: I think it makes you think a little deeper about what shoes you wear.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它会让你更深入地思考该穿什么鞋。

sentences.en: Because I do have pants that seem to swallow a lower profile shoe.
sentences.zh: 因为我确实有那种看起来会把低帮鞋“吞掉”的裤子。

sentences.en: But I like the cleanliness of a broader pant and how straight that line feels along the side.
sentences.zh: 但我喜欢宽裤子的利落感，以及侧面那条直线的感觉。

sentences.en: And I think that that looks nice.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那样看起来很好看。

sentences.en: I just think it looks very sharp.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得它看起来非常干练。

sentences.en: And you look, particularly like for the workday, it's in this moment where suits are really, have long faded and ties are really endangered.
sentences.zh: 而且你看，特别是在工作日，现在这个时代，西装早已没落，领带也濒临灭绝。

sentences.en: I think it's a way to look like clean and crisp and a little traditional without having to really modify your entire outfit.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一种看起来干净利落、带点传统感，又不必彻底改变全身装束的方法。

sentences.en: I do know that the minute you switch, fashion will change because that's what happens, right?
sentences.zh: 我确实知道，你一换风格，时尚就会变，因为这就是时尚，对吧？

sentences.en: This is a pendulum.
sentences.zh: 这是一个钟摆。

sentences.en: It is cyclical.
sentences.zh: 它是循环往复的。

sentences.en: What if I leave this booth right now and go buy a pair of double pleated trousers?
sentences.zh: 如果我现在离开这个展位去买一条双褶长裤会怎样？

sentences.en: That means like in three months from now, flat trousers will be back.
sentences.zh: 那意味着三个月后，平前襟长裤又会流行回来。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Is that the laws of the universe here?
sentences.zh: 这是宇宙法则吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, the laws of the fashion universe.
sentences.zh: 是的，时尚界的宇宙法则。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: And when we return, we are going to end our episode as we do every week with a little game.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将像每周一样，以一个小游戏结束我们的节目。

sentences.en: I'm Winnaloo.
sentences.zh: 我是Winnaloo。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《Connections》，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是Sam Mazursky，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问nytimes.com/games，今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Every week we play a game, and the time to play that game is now.
sentences.zh: 每周我们都会玩个游戏，现在就是玩游戏的时间了。

sentences.en: And I promise the two of you, it's not going to be silly.
sentences.zh: 我向你们两位保证，这不会很傻。

sentences.en: Maybe it'll be a little silly, but that's fine.
sentences.zh: 也许会有一点点傻，但没关系。

sentences.en: Let's roll with it.
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧。

sentences.en: We've talked about all kinds of fashion today, but this quiz is about a piece of clothing that I think pretty much everyone has worn at some point in their lives.
sentences.zh: 今天我们聊了各种时尚，但这个小测验是关于一件我觉得几乎每个人一生中都穿过的衣服。

sentences.en: This quiz is about jeans, skinny jeans, baggy jeans.
sentences.zh: 这个测验是关于牛仔裤的，紧身牛仔裤，宽松牛仔裤。

sentences.en: You love them.
sentences.zh: 你爱它们。

sentences.en: You hate them.
sentences.zh: 你恨它们。

sentences.en: We've talked about them.
sentences.zh: 我们聊过它们。

sentences.en: They've been part of the American wardrobe for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 它们在美式衣橱里已经存在很长时间了。

sentences.en: And so how the game is going to work is we have three rounds here, and they're all focused on jeans in some way.
sentences.zh: 所以游戏规则是这样的，我们有三轮，每一轮都以某种方式围绕牛仔裤展开。

sentences.en: It's a little bit of genealogy.
